startup.recommendedDesign:
GOAL: list every autostart source, let the user toggle it exactly the way Task Manager does, never delete anything, journal the previous raw state.

1. SOURCES TO LIST (read-only first)
 a) HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run (64-bit view), and HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\...\Run (32-bit view).
 b) User Startup folder (shell:startup) and common Startup folder (shell:common startup).
 c) Packaged apps with a StartupTask (read AppxManifest.xml, state from HKCU\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\AppModel\SystemAppData\<PackageFamilyName>\<TaskId>\State; optimizerDuck StartupManagerService.cs:268,359-364. RyTuneX reads <pkg>\StartupTask\<TaskId> instead (StartupHelper.cs:241-252): the two layouts are NOT reconciled, verify on the live machine).
 d) Scheduled tasks with a logon or boot trigger that are not under \Microsoft\Windows\ (user and vendor updaters). Toggle with the Task Scheduler API Enabled flag and journal the previous value.
 e) Auto-start services belong to the Services page, not here. RunOnce, Winlogon Shell/Userinit, Active Setup, AppInit, Policies\Explorer\Run, BHO are shown read-only or not at all (no approval mechanism exists for them).

2. STARTUPAPPROVED BINARY LAYOUT (undocumented by Microsoft; reconstructed from 5 tools)
 Keys (value name = the Run value name, or the file name WITH extension for the Startup folder):
   <hive>\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\StartupApproved\Run         for Run entries
   <hive>\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\StartupApproved\Run32       for Wow6432Node Run entries (optimizerDuck :183, RyTuneX :13, WinTune :86)
   <hive>\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\StartupApproved\StartupFolder for Startup folder items (HKCU = user folder, HKLM = common folder; RyTuneX :14-15, WinTune :90-91)
 Value type REG_BINARY, 12 bytes:
   bytes 0-3  little-endian DWORD status. 0x02 = enabled (default written when re-enabled), 0x03 = disabled by the user. Variants 0x06 / 0x07 are seen as enabled / disabled (optimizerDuck :208-210 lists 02,06 enabled and 03,07 disabled; WinTune preserves the variant when toggling, StartupManager.ahk:322-336).
   bytes 4-11 FILETIME (UTC, 100 ns ticks since 1601, little-endian) of the moment the item was disabled; Task Manager shows it as the disable date. All zero when enabled (WindowsMize Set-OneDriveRunAtStartup.ps1:35-42; optimizerDuck writes the time in both states, RyTuneX writes zeros in both: both are tolerated).
 Decoding rule that satisfies all five tools: value missing = enabled; byte0 even (0x00, 0x02, 0x06) = enabled; byte0 odd (0x01, 0x03, 0x07) = disabled. Differences: AutoDarkMode RegistryHandler.cs:484-488 treats 0 and 2 as approved; RyTuneX :455-457 treats any odd as disabled; optimizerDuck only 03/07 as disabled; WinTune any odd. Use the "odd = disabled" rule but never rewrite a byte0 value you do not understand (keep it in the journal and leave the entry read-only).
 VERIFIED: the layout of bytes 0-3 and the 12-byte length (all five tools agree, and two of them write the same bytes WindowsMize/optimizerDuck/WinTune). NOT VERIFIED on a live Windows 11 registry: (i) which hive Task Manager reads/writes for an HKLM Run item (RyTuneX, WinTune and optimizerDuck assume HKLM\...\StartupApproved\Run, which needs admin; the safe assumption for a per-user app is HKCU); (ii) whether a missing Run32 value means disabled on Windows 11 (optimizerDuck claims it; nothing else does); (iii) meaning of byte0 values other than 02/03/06/07; (iv) the packaged-app State path (see 1c).
 CALIBRATION STEP before shipping (read-only, one minute): on the target Windows build toggle one HKLM Run item (for example "SecurityHealth") and one HKCU Run item in Task Manager > Startup apps, diff both StartupApproved\Run keys before and after, and store the result as a test fixture.

3. TOGGLE ALGORITHM (reversible, journaled)
 - Read the current raw state (bytes or "absent") from every candidate key; write it to the journal before touching anything.
 - Disable: write 12 bytes { 03 00 00 00 } + FILETIME(now) to the key that Task Manager uses for that source (HKCU unless calibration shows HKLM is required, then use the elevated helper). If the current byte0 is 0x06 write 0x07, keep the variant.
 - Enable: write { 02 00 00 00 } + 8 zero bytes (or 06 if the variant was 06); or restore the exact journaled bytes; if the journal says "absent", delete only the StartupApproved value that WinModes created.
 - Never delete or edit Run values, shortcuts or StartupApproved keys (TairikuOokami deletes the whole StartupApproved tree, RyTuneX/WinTune/Winrift/Win11Debloat delete Run values; all of that is irreversible and the item vanishes from Task Manager).
 - Packaged StartupTask: Microsoft states DisabledByUser "can only be re-enabled by the user" (StartupTaskState Learn page), so a registry State write is outside the API contract: offer disable only, mark re-enable as "ask the user to enable it in Settings > Apps > Startup", re-read the State after the write.
 - Scheduled-task startup items: use ITaskService Enabled=false and journal the previous Enabled flag; do not use schtasks text parsing (localised output).
 - After each write re-read through the same decoder and compare; report failure instead of assuming.

4. SAFETY RULES
 - Hard blocklist (never show a toggle): SecurityHealth (Windows Security tray), anything in protected.json user-apps unless the user put the app in the active profile, input-method hosts (ctfmon, TextInputHost), audio and GPU control services/tray hosts (Realtek, NVIDIA container), edge WebView2 helpers, OneDrive only with the known-folder/sync check from the OneDrive feature.
 - Entries that are not under the current user (HKLM, common folder) need the elevated helper and the same journal under %ProgramData%\WinModes.
 - Show source, command line, publisher and signature; never run or probe the target executable.
 - Keep the existing "StartupAppTask" scheduled task alone: it is the Windows notification that tells the user about many startup apps and is harmless.

traps.title: Internet Connection Sharing (SharedAccess) set to Disabled
traps.detail: winutil "Services - Set to Manual" sets SharedAccess to Disabled with a wrong OriginalType of Automatic (Default is Manual); vukilis copies it; WindowsMize disables it. ICS is the NAT engine under WSL2, Hyper-V Default Switch, Docker Desktop and Mobile Hotspot. WindowsMize itself notes WSL2 resets it to Manual.

traps.title: Hyper-V / WSL host services disabled by a default preset
traps.detail: WindowsMize's default script enables the "HyperV" group: HvHost and vmcompute become Disabled (its own comment says vmcompute is "needed by WSL"), plus the "Miscellaneous" group disables P9RdrService (\\wsl$ file access) and the "Network" group disables SharedAccess and iphlpsvc (netsh portproxy, IPv6 transition). Running that preset breaks WSL2/Docker. GTweak's HyperV toggle disables HvHost and all vmic* too. None of the tools mention LxssManager/WSLService/vmms, so they cannot be protected by name.

traps.title: Microsoft Store / winget stack disabled as a group
traps.detail: GTweak's "WindowsStore" toggle sets WalletService, VacSvc, spectrum, SharedRealitySvc, perceptionsimulation, MixedRealityOpenXRSvc, MapsBroker, EntAppSvc, embeddedmode, wlidsvc, WEPHOSTSVC, StorSvc, ClipSVC and InstallService to Disabled through TrustedInstaller. The last four plus wlidsvc make Store apps unlicensed/uninstallable and break winget msstore and App Installer updates. Sycnex disables InstallService in its Sysprep path, privacy.sexy offers wlidsvc (strict), Win10BloatRemover disables the Clip\License Validation task.

traps.title: Windows Update "disable" tweaks go far beyond a start type
traps.detail: winutil stops and disables BITS, wuauserv and UsoSvc, wipes C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution and disables six task folders by wildcard. Winhance also disables WaaSMedicSvc, rewrites sc failure actions to none and renames WaaSMedicSvc.dll and wuaueng.dll in System32 (takeown + icacls Everyone:F). RyTuneX takes ownership of the WaaSMedicSvc registry key and sets DisableWindowsUpdateAccess. GTweak sets DoSvc/UsoSvc/wuauserv/WaaSMedicSvc to 4 and the NoAutoUpdate policies. Result: no security patches, no Store/winget msstore updates, optional-feature, .NET and WSL kernel installs fail. Folder wildcards also disable tasks that Windows adds later.

traps.title: Edge Update services and WebView2 update tasks disabled
traps.detail: privacy.sexy (standard level), RyTuneX, GTweak, Batlez and Winrift disable edgeupdate/edgeupdatem; RyTuneX also disables MicrosoftEdgeUpdateTaskMachine* and the WebView2 update tasks. Edge and the WebView2 Runtime then stop receiving security updates; Claude/Codex style WebView2 apps keep running on a stale runtime. protected.json already lists edgeupdate and edgeupdatem. Note privacy.sexy ships this at "standard" because it assumes the user does not want Edge.

traps.title: Per-user service templates and wildcard names
traps.detail: Services such as CDPUserSvc, OneSyncSvc, cbdhsvc, UserDataSvc, UnistoreSvc, MessagingService, BcastDVRUserService, webthreatdefusersvc, P9RdrService exist as a template key plus per-logon instances named <name>_<LUID>. The old winutil list (copied by sparkle and others) passes names like "CDPUserSvc_*" to Set-Service -Name, which does not take wildcards, so each entry just logs a warning; changing only an instance reverts at next logon. The change must go to the template (HKLM\...\Services\<name>\Start) and applies from the next sign-in; the journal must key on the template name.
evidence: sparkle tweaks/set-services-to-manual/apply.ps1:3-284 (wildcard names in the list; Set-Service loop at the end of the file)

traps.title: Hard-coded "restore default" values are wrong or inconsistent
traps.detail: The default of one service differs between projects: UsoSvc Automatic (winutil Invoke-WPFUpdatesdefault.ps1:67, privacy.sexy, Winhance UpdateService.cs:168) vs Manual (Microsoft IoT table, ZOICWARE zFunctions.psm1:8313, RemoveWindowsAI :3957, Pavise-Rescue.cmd); BITS Manual (Microsoft IoT, WindowsMize) vs Automatic-delayed (sparkle, RyTuneX :1443-1444); wuauserv Manual vs Auto (Winhance UpdateService.cs:167); DoSvc Automatic-delayed (RyTuneX restore) vs Automatic (privacy.sexy, Microsoft IoT) vs Manual (WindowsMize export). RyTuneX "restore telemetry" writes Start=2 to 13 services including TrkWks, whesvc, InventorySvc whatever their real default was (OptimizeSystemHelper.cs:826-845). winutil sets "wermgr" (an executable, not a service) so that tweak is a silent no-op (config/tweaks.json:546), and the SharedAccess OriginalType is wrong. WinModes must always restore the journaled original (ServiceTuner already does) and never a constant; the delayed-auto flag has to be restored too (RyTuneX writes DelayedAutostart manually, :1438,1444).

traps.title: Deleting services or their registry keys
traps.detail: Win10BloatRemover runs sc delete (after exporting the key) for DiagTrack, diagsvc, diagnosticshub.standardcollector.service, PcaSvc, dmwappushservice, DmEnrollmentSvc, RetailDemo, TroubleshootingSvc, UCPD, wisvc and, after taking ownership, for DPS, WdiSystemHost, WdiServiceHost. GTweak deletes the whole DiagTrack, dmwappushservice and diagsvc key trees and rebuilds them from hard-coded values on revert. Not reversible by a Start value; System File Checker or an in-place upgrade is needed to get them back. WinModes must only change Start (and never touch the ACL).

traps.title: Bypassing the service protection of Windows (registry writes, ACL takeover)
traps.detail: Since Windows 10 1809 some services (DoSvc, WaaSMedicSvc, AppIDSvc, Defender and firewall services) reject SCM changes with Access is denied. privacy.sexy has a DisableServiceInRegistry function for them, winutil writes AppIDSvc Start straight into the registry, RyTuneX takes ownership of the WaaSMedicSvc key, GTweak and Win10BloatRemover run as TrustedInstaller. A WinModes ServiceTuner that gets "Access is denied" must report it and stop, never escalate: these are exactly the never-touch services.

traps.title: Core shell services set to Disabled or Manual
traps.detail: WindowsMize disables Themes (visual styles) and FontCache/FontCache3.0.0.0 in its default "Miscellaneous" group; GTweak offers MMCSS Disabled (audio/video scheduler); ET-Optimizer sets Manual on SamSs, StateRepository, TextInputManagementService, TokenBroker, TimeBrokerSvc, AppXSvc, SecurityHealthService, Sense, StorSvc, TabletInputService, BITS, UsoSvc; WindowsMize documents TextInputManagementService as "DO NOT DISABLE (system will fail to boot)" and WpnUserService/DevicesFlowUserSvc as DO NOT DISABLE. ZOICWARE's "all services to manual" keeps a hand-curated Automatic list (AudioEndpointBuilder, Audiosrv, EventLog, SysMain, Themes, WSearch, NVDisplay.ContainerLocalSystem, WlanSvc, BFE, BrokerInfrastructure, CoreMessagingRegistrar, Dnscache, LSM, mpssvc, RpcEptMapper, Schedule, SystemEventsBroker, StateRepository, TextInputManagementService, sppsvc) which is a good seed for a "never below Automatic" list.

traps.title: TabletInputService "disable" renames a system executable
traps.detail: Winhance's recommended option for TabletInputService also sets IsInputAppPreloadEnabled=0 and, on Win11 without a CJK language, takes ownership and renames C:\Windows\SystemApps\MicrosoftWindows.Client.CBS_cw5n1h2txyewy\TextInputHost.exe to .old.exe. That breaks the emoji panel (Win+.), touch keyboard, IME candidate windows and clipboard-history UI, and a renamed SystemApps file can fail servicing. A start-type change alone is enough and safer.

traps.title: Volume Shadow Copy / restore points disabled by a default preset
traps.detail: WindowsMize enables the "WindowsBackupAndSystemRestore" group by default: VSS, swprv, wbengine, SDRSVC, CloudBackupRestoreSvc go Disabled and the SystemRestore SR task too. GTweak disables wbengine/swprv/vds/ and System Restore. RemoveWindowsAI and ZOICWARE must flip VSS back to Manual just to create a restore point. WinModes should keep VSS/swprv Manual so it can create a restore point before risky changes.

traps.title: Scheduled tasks that look like noise but do real work
traps.detail: Winrift disables \Microsoft\Windows\Defrag\ScheduledDefrag which also issues the scheduled TRIM on SSDs; WindowsMize disables the .NET Framework NGEN tasks (slower first start of .NET Framework apps, relevant on a dev PC), RegIdleBackup (registry backup safety net), SystemRestore\SR, StartComponentCleanup and SilentCleanup (WindowsMize marks the last two as SkipTask); Win10BloatRemover disables Clip\License Validation and License Manager\TempSignedLicenseExchange (Store licences); RyTuneX disables GameInput and GameDVR tasks together with GameInputSvc. Folder wildcards (WaaSMedic, UpdateOrchestrator, InstallService) catch tasks Windows adds later.

traps.title: Startup managers that delete state
traps.detail: TairikuOokami deletes the whole StartupApproved tree under HKCU and HKLM (every item disabled in Task Manager re-enables on next logon). RyTuneX "Remove" and WinTune "Delete" remove the Run value or Startup shortcut and the StartupApproved value, so the item is gone from Task Manager and cannot be re-enabled. Winrift removes the HKCU Run OneDriveSetup value. Use StartupApproved writes only.

traps.title: Security-center / firewall services killed by "privacy" tools
traps.detail: Windows-On-Reins disables MpsSvc and Defender services, TairikuOokami and awesome-windows11 disable WinDefend/Sense/WdNisSvc/SecurityHealthService, privacy.sexy has WinDefend, MpsSvc, wscsvc, SecurityHealthService, Sense, webthreatdefsvc under non-recommended categories, ET-Optimizer sets SecurityHealthService/Sense to Manual. Out of scope for WinModes (project invariant), keep out of the catalog.

traps.title: SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB written to total RAM
traps.detail: winutil's Services tweak and sparkle also set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB to the installed RAM size so services share fewer svchost.exe. A crash or hang of one service then takes down every service in that shared host and process-level diagnostics get coarser. It is a registry value, not a start type; keep it out of the services page.

traps.title: WSearch / SysMain / Spooler "disabled for speed" without a hardware check
traps.detail: Winhance and RyTuneX disable SysMain with a warning that it hurts HDD systems; WSearch disabled makes Start, Explorer and Outlook search return nothing (Winhance warning at :1340); Spooler disabled removes printing and Print to PDF. Memory compression is NOT SysMain (Pavise-Rescue restores it with Enable-MMAgent separately) and must never be touched (protected.json). Offer these as opt-in with the check (system drive is SSD, no printer installed).

traps.title: Third-party and driver services mixed into Windows lists
traps.detail: TweakList disables NVDisplay.ContainerLocalSystem (needed by the NVIDIA Control Panel); ZOICWARE keeps it Automatic; WindowsMize's Intel group disables IntelAudioService (HDMI/DP audio), cplspcon/cphs (DRM, premium video), igccservice and Thunderbolt services (its comments warn). GTweak deletes nothing but offers AdobeARM, gupdate, edgeupdate in the same list as Windows services. The WinModes third-party.json already separates vendor services; keep that separation.

traps.title: Winhance "default option" markers are not Windows defaults
traps.detail: In Winhance's service comboboxes the item flagged IsDefault is sometimes not the Windows default (MixedRealityOpenXRSvc default flagged Disabled, TabletInputService/SysMain/Spooler/WSearch/DiagTrack flagged Automatic whether or not Windows uses Delayed). Use it as a hint only; read the live original with ServiceTuner.

notes:
DEFAULTS: microsoftDefault comes first from the Microsoft Learn Windows IoT Enterprise service table (applies to Windows 11 IoT Enterprise, updated 2026-06; it is not the client SKU, so a few values differ), else from the WindowsMize export of a Windows 11 machine (DefaultType), else from the privacy.sexy Windows 11 tables. All three raw values are in defaultSources; defaultsDisagree=true marks real conflicts (for example BITS, DoSvc, UsoSvc, NlaSvc, RemoteRegistry, SecurityHealthService, mpssvc, WSearch, PcaSvc, MapsBroker, wscsvc). I did NOT guess a value when none of the three sources lists the service ("unknown"). WinModes must read the live original and journal it, never trust a constant.

GUIDANCE TABLE: the Microsoft table also gives a recommendation per service (OK to disable / Do not disable / No guidance). It is written for locked-down IoT devices: it says OK to disable for ClipSVC, AppXSvc, InstallService, wlidsvc, LanmanServer, iphlpsvc, Themes, which WinModes must NOT follow because of Store/winget/WSL/UI dependencies.

VERDICT KEY: safe-manual = Manual (and Disabled if the feature is unused) loses nothing the user needs; safe-on-demand-only = keep Manual (demand/trigger start) but do not offer Disabled because some app can request it (Store, Xbox, VPN, smart card, Bluetooth, RDP, VSS); leave = no worthwhile gain or the projects disagree, offer only as an explicit opt-in; never = no mode or tweak may change it.

COUNTS: projectsSet lists every project/target pair found. independentVotes/disabledVotes/manualVotes merge copies into one vote: winutil, sparkle, vukilis and optimizerDuck share the legacy winutil list; privacy.sexy and Winrift share one list. Many Manual votes only restate the default (the "set to manual" lists), so rank by disabledVotes plus the "why", not by raw counts. WindowsMize is the author's personal preset (groups can be commented out, see the note on each entry), Winhance lists the recommended option of a combobox (it is not applied unless chosen), Win11Debloat and Sophia are the most conservative (Win11Debloat: one service; Sophia: DiagTrack and WerSvc).

SERVICE LIST SIZE: 120 services kept out of about 370 distinct names seen in 25 projects; entries were removed when the service is Disabled-by-default or a no-op Manual with a single vote (vmicheartbeat, NetTcpPortSharing, UevAgentService, uhssvc, shpamsvc, RemoteAccess, DialogBlockingService, PrintNotify, SmsRouter, SstpSvc, lltdsvc, PeerDistSvc, upnphost, wbengine, AppVClient, AJRouter, SDRSVC, fhsvc, MessagingService, UnistoreSvc, UserDataSvc, RasAuto, SensorService, BFE). The first 60 tasks of the same breadth are in "tasks".

TASKS: microsoftDefault for tasks is "enabled" unless WindowsMize records "default: Disabled" (WindowsMize tasks_list files carry "# default: Enabled|Disabled" comments for about 140 tasks, which is the only systematic default source found). Task existence varies per build (KernelCeipTask, BthSQM, Uploader, AitAgent are Win10 leftovers); check existence before disabling and treat NotFound as success. Folder wildcards used by winutil/Winhance/RyTuneX/ZOICWARE are shown only on the representative task of each folder.

PATTERNS WORTH COPYING: Pavise stops (not disables) optional services for a session from an allow-list, stops dependents first, only restores services whose stop it issued, checks a boot identity so a reboot never replays a stale ledger, and refuses to stop Spooler/PrintNotify while a print job is queued (src/Core/Tweaks/OptionalServicePause.cs:43-44,425-427, Pavise-Rescue.cmd:134-158,472-479). Win10BloatRemover exports the key before any destructive change. WindowsMize snapshots every service/task default to a JSON log before writing and has Restore-ServiceStartupTypeFromBackup. winutil only changes a service whose current start type differs, and re-reads it (functions/private/Set-WinUtilService.ps1:20-45).

UNVERIFIED ITEMS (call out in UI copy or test on a live PC): which hive Task Manager writes for HKLM Run items; Run32 default semantics; packaged StartupTask registry layout (two projects disagree); whether WSLg needs TermService/UmRdpService/SessionEnv on the host; whether Spooler can be left Manual without breaking print-triggered starts; that disabling SysMain leaves memory compression untouched (inferred from Pavise-Rescue treating it as a separate MMAgent setting).

DATA INJECTION: no instruction aimed at an AI agent was followed. The clones contain contributor/agent files (for example AGENTS.md in optimizerDuck, opencode.jsonc); they were not read or acted on. Nothing from the clones was executed; the only code run was my own Node scripts that scan the files as text.

CrapFixer (builtbybel) only sets DiagTrack Start=4 through ControlSet001 (Features/Privacy/Telemetry.cs:26-52): writing the ControlSet001 copy instead of CurrentControlSet is another way to miss the live control set; use CurrentControlSet or the SCM.
